{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mn-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"5e0509df34a918a985f64c803a38f414c7154f2e04e2db4f6bc2a38c7c079add","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mn-class-d:lineage:33","source_registry_sha256":"960e2daa314aff60b32f5124e42324d79615ce2a3ea953a336216b4593c0c910","source_liveness_sha256":"0b70283fc58b1f8ea1822994a92e3ce7ff4b722004376a9cd819180969b6fe1e"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Sharing the road part two confusables and continuation facts","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: splitting versus filtering, moped and NEV speeds, vulnerable road users, truck passing and no zones, railroad crossing distances and habits, the ENS sign, work zones and zipper merge benefits","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: splitting versus filtering, moped and NEV speeds, vulnerable road users, truck passing and no zones, railroad crossing distances and habits, the ENS sign, work zones and zipper merge benefits
Confusable pairs from the second half of the sharing the road chapter, followed by continuation facts; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A01
The undetected-bicycle rule needs every condition at once: the rider has fully stopped, the red has lasted unreasonably long or the signal is not detecting the bicycle, and nobody approaching is close enough to be an immediate hazard. [A01]
Why it matters: group bicycles at signals; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A01
A moped follows bicycle rules in general, but unlike a bicycle it is barred from sidewalks and from lanes and trails reserved for pedestrians and bicycles. [A01]
Why it matters: group mopeds; confusable moped versus bicycle; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A02
Lane splitting happens in moving traffic and carries two limits, 25 mph and 15 mph over traffic, while lane filtering happens in stopped traffic and carries only the 15 mph over traffic limit. [A02]
Why it matters: group motorcycles; confusable splitting versus filtering; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A02
Motorcycles do not protect riders in a crash the way other vehicles protect their occupants. [A02]
Why it matters: group motorcycles; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A03
Vulnerable road users have no seat belts or airbags and face a higher risk of injury in a crash, and they must follow all traffic laws themselves. [A03]
Why it matters: group vulnerable road users; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A03
You must share the road safely with vulnerable road users on highways, bikeways, sidewalks and trails, and with any passengers they carry. [A03]
Why it matters: group vulnerable road users; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A03
A neighborhood electric vehicle's own top speed falls between 20 and 25 mph, while the streets it may use must be posted at 35 mph or less. [A03]
Why it matters: group NEVs; confusable vehicle speed versus street limit; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A03
Before passing a commercial vehicle, make sure you have safe clearance beside, behind and ahead of your vehicle. [A03]
Why it matters: group passing trucks; prereq for the passing steps.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A04
A truck driver may not see you up to 20 feet in front of the cab but up to 200 feet behind the trailer, so the rear no zone is ten times longer than the front one. [A04]
Why it matters: group no zones; confusable front versus rear distance; difficulty high.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A04
In a turn, a vehicle's back wheels track inside the path of its front wheels, and that gap grows with the length of the vehicle. [A04]
Why it matters: group wide turns; explains the open space a truck leaves on its right.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-R11 | anchor: A04
A turning truck may leave an open space on its right just before turning, so watch its turn signals closely. [A04]
Why it matters: group wide turns; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-R12 | anchor: A04
Keeping a safe distance behind a commercial vehicle also gives you time to react if it stops suddenly. [A04]
Why it matters: group following trucks; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-R13 | anchor: A05
Trucks and buses run under operating restrictions and may use speed limiters, and honking, aggressive driving or weaving around them only adds dangerous distractions. [A05]
Why it matters: group patience; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-R14 | anchor: A05
Warning signs and pavement markings tell you a railroad crossing is ahead, and signs near the track show how many tracks there are. [A05]
Why it matters: group railroad warnings; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-R15 | anchor: A05
At a crossing the first ten-foot rule is where you stop, short of the nearest rail or gate, and the second is where you must be able to clear, beyond the far rail, before you start across. [A05]
Why it matters: group railroad distances; confusable stop distance versus clearing distance; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-R16 | anchor: A05
When traffic is heavy on both sides of a crossing, wait behind the tracks until you can get all the way across, and never race a train. [A05]
Why it matters: group railroad safety; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-R17 | anchor: A05
Trains cannot stop as quickly as cars, and their speed and distance are hard to judge, especially at night, so if you hesitate with a train in sight, stop and let it pass. [A05]
Why it matters: group railroad safety; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-R18 | anchor: A05
Motorcyclists should approach railroad crossings with caution and should not swerve for a better crossing angle, which can put them into oncoming traffic. [A05]
Why it matters: group railroad safety; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-R19 | anchor: A05
Treat a flag person at a railroad crossing the same way you would treat a warning device, and never stop on the tracks. [A05]
Why it matters: group railroad safety; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-R20 | anchor: A06
Giving the number on the blue ENS sign lets dispatchers pinpoint the crossing and tell trains headed that way to stop or slow down. [A06]
Why it matters: group ENS; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-R21 | anchor: A06
Work zones may have machinery moving or parked at any hour, so be patient, expect delays at peak times and follow the signs and markings workers set up. [A06]
Why it matters: group work zones; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-R22 | anchor: A06
Stay alert in a work zone and shift your lane position to keep away from workers and equipment, because lanes may be changed and distractions can be fatal. [A06]
Why it matters: group work zones; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-R23 | anchor: A06
Drivers have traditionally been taught to merge early, but early merging leads to longer backups, more crashes and more road rage. [A06]
Why it matters: group zipper merge; confusable early versus late merge; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-R24 | anchor: A06
When traffic is heavy and slow, staying in your current lane until the point where drivers can take turns is the safer choice. [A06]
Why it matters: group zipper merge; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-R25 | anchor: A07
The zipper merge can shorten traffic backups by up to 40 percent. [A07]
Why it matters: group zipper merge; the one number on the benefits page.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec08-R26 | anchor: A07
Zipper merging also improves worker safety in lane closures, narrows the speed gap between lanes, eases congestion at freeway interchanges, feels fairer and cuts road rage. [A07]
Why it matters: group zipper merge; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0058]
